topics.title: Stuttering Interviewer Takes Calls
topics.summary: The broadcast features an interviewer named Mel who frequently stutters while discussing his appearance and accomplishments. He plays music from his own band, Josie Seng, and attempts to engage callers, including one individual detailing a past romantic encounter centered around perceived physical unattractiveness.

topics.title: Radio Broadcast with Josie and Led Zeppelin
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, host John plays ‘Too Late for Love’ by Josie followed by music from Led Zeppelin including 'Heartbreaker'. A caller discusses his wife’s stuttering while another inquires about equipment choices between K-Rock and YSP.

topics.title: New Intern Discusses Broadcast
topics.summary: A new radio intern named Mike discusses his experiences during a broadcast featuring Howard Stern. He recounts conversations with callers including one obsessed with The Kinks’ ‘Living on a Thin Line,’ shares weather updates, and attempts to play an original bit about Gary Delabate.

topics.title: Gary Delabate’s Absurd Phone Call
topics.summary: During a radio segment, host Gary Delabate engages in an increasingly bizarre phone call filled with nonsensical requests—including potato-related tasks and impersonations of rock stars—while struggling with apparent distress. The conversation devolves into chaotic exchanges involving personal details about deceased relatives and confusing academic references.” 2 sentences, 54 words.

topics.title: Ribs and Josie Sang a Song
topics.summary: A radio host presents a comedic bit about ribs invented by Wilma Flintstone, soliciting listener calls for club recommendations. The segment transitions to an original song "Morning Sun" performed by Josie Sang, exploring themes of lost love and remembrance.

topics.title: Summer Music, Commercial Breaks, and Caller Interaction
topics.summary: During this broadcast, segments included an extended musical performance featuring 'Rock On,' followed by commercials for Kawasaki watercrafts and McDonald’s. A lengthy call-in segment featured callers discussing personal experiences including a conversation about Captain Jank and various topics before concluding with repeated phrases regarding the popularity of music.
